newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks rise, sharp pick-up in trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks rise, sharp pick-up in trade.

text.p: Argentine stocks finished higher Tuesday, the market's third consecutive rise, amid a sharp pick up in trading volumes.
Traders said there was some selling late in the session which prevented the market from rising even more.
The blue-chip Merval stock index rose 1.11 percent to 635.65 points.
"The market is going through an excellent moment. The main trigger is the abundance of liquidity circulating in the market," said Jose Napoli, a trader at brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
Traders said the Merval is now heading for 650, spurred by a rebound in Argentine economic growth, high international liquidity levels and lower U.S. Treasury bond yields.

Traders noted a sharp pick-up in activity, with some 39.9 million pesos worth of shares changing hands, more than twice as much as on Monday. Trade of this magnitude has not been reported since May 21.
"There was a large off-loading of positions, above all in the stocks that have given the best yields in recent weeks," Napoli said.
The Merval hit a high of 640.44 points Tuesday, representing a rise of 1.88 percent.
Another trader noted that the higher trade volumes represented genuine buying, "although some players continue to maintain that a correction is necessary.
Of 73 stocks traded this session, 52 rose, eight declined and the rest remained flat.
